title: Joining John's dance and brass bands
summary: Williams describes joining John's dance band in 1957 and brass band in 1958-59 and who played in it.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. When did you start in with John? Hasn't it?

I started playing with John, I think I was in the hospital in 57. I started playing with his dance band around 57. Mm-hmm. And started playing with his brass band, must have been around 58 to 59. Mm-hmm.
So, who would he have in his dance band when you first joined?

Vernon Gilbert. And me, him, Vernon Gilbert, Tillman. Playing what? Tillman playing bass, you know. Mm-hmm. Bass horn, you know, like he playing the Vernon Gilbert trumpet. You know, clarinet. And, um, well, he had a saxophonian, Handy playing with him. Pretty good while, Handy playing with him a good while. Um, and after Handy stopped playing with him, and I had Harold. Mm-hmm. Harold been playing with him. He was Smitty on piano. And he used the piano, you know what I'm saying? Did he use a guitar player ordinarily, or did he? He had Clifford Brown. No Clifford. He was a Clifford guitar player.
That's not the same as Raymond Clifford. No, no.
He's another Clifford Brown. He stayed downtown. It's in Antony Street. That was his regular guitar player. Clifford. I see. So he's changed up some to his band now.
Yeah, well, he used Sales, you see. He had an outside job in Sales, he was playing Harold.
Still got Harold and used Anderson, you see. Been using Anderson now about two years.
Oh, he still uses Harold when he had to call for that very good piece.
He played up at the fraternity house in 5018, last Saturday. The Saturday that I played with Jim, you see.
No, on St. Charles. On St. Charles. Yeah, you know, on that side, big house on that side.

I played the first dance with him, when the first, second week after school opened. We all played, but last Saturday before last, while I was playing down there, you see, for your own. So you got Sun White to play.
